async def act(page):
    import asyncio
    # Locate the filter row in the customer table
    # The filter row is in the second rowgroup of the table with the filter elements
    # Use the table that contains the header row with 'ID Name Email Group Telephone ...'
    # We can filter the table by looking for a row with 'Any' in it (as per the tree)
    filter_row = page.get_by_role('row').filter(has=page.get_by_role('cell', name='Any'))
    # Get the fifth cell in this row (corresponding to the Telephone column)
    # Indexing: first cell is 'Any', second is 'From: . To : .', third is '.', fourth is '.', fifth is the Telephone textbox
    telephone_cell = filter_row.get_by_role('cell').nth(4)  # zero-based index, so 4 is the fifth cell
    # Find the textbox within this cell
    telephone_textbox = telephone_cell.get_by_role('textbox')
    # Fill the textbox with the phone number
    await telephone_textbox.fill('2065555555')
    # Click the 'Search' button to apply the filter
    await page.get_by_role('button', name='Search').click()
    # Wait for the page to update; use networkidle to ensure all requests are done
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    # Add a short sleep to ensure the UI updates
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    # Now, check the customer rows for the phone number 2065555555
    # The customer rows are in the rowgroup after the filter row
    # We can locate all rows that contain customer data (they have cells with IDs like '209', '208', etc.)
    # But to be precise, we can look for a cell with the exact text '2065555555' in the Telephone column
    # First, find the table again after the search
    customer_table = page.get_by_role('table').filter(has=page.get_by_role('cell', name='ID'))
    # Get all rows in the table that are not the header or filter rows
    # The header row has 'ID Name Email ...', and the filter row has 'Any From: ...'
    # We can skip the first two rows (header and filter) and check the rest
    rows = customer_table.get_by_role('row').all()
    # Iterate through rows to find the one with the phone number
    for row in rows:
        # Get the cells in this row
        cells = row.get_by_role('cell').all()
        if len(cells) >= 5:  # Ensure it has at least the Telephone column (fifth cell)
            telephone_cell = cells[4]  # Fifth cell is Telephone (zero-based index 4)
            telephone_text = await telephone_cell.text_content()
            if telephone_text.strip() == '2065555555':
                # Found the row, extract name and email
                name_cell = cells[2]  # Third cell is Name (zero-based index 2)
                email_cell = cells[3]  # Fourth cell is Email (zero-based index 3)
                name = (await name_cell.text_content()).strip()
                email = (await email_cell.text_content()).strip()
                # Return the result as a string in the required format
                return f"Name: {name}, Email: {email}"
    # If no row found, return a message
    return "No customer found with phone number 2065555555."
